title: Model Charges for Photoshoot in India: Fees, Usage and Releases

children.text: What brand managers and agency producers should agree with models before a shoot, from day rates and overtime to usage tiers, buyouts and release forms, so a catalogue image never becomes a billboard dispute.

layout.content: Model Charges for Photoshoot in India: Fees, Usage and Releases

A catalogue shoot is approved, the images look great, and three months later the performance team puts one in a paid ad and the media team wants it on a billboard. Then the model's agency gets in touch. Most disputes like this are not about the day rate. They happen because nobody wrote down what the images could be used for, where and for how long. This guide covers model charges for photoshoot in India as they are typically quoted, how usage buyouts work, what a model release should say and what brand managers and agency producers should agree in writing before the studio is booked.
This is general information, not legal advice. Have a lawyer review your standard model agreement and release before you rely on them.
Typical model day rates in India
Rates vary widely by experience, city, agency, category and the brand's profile. Model platforms and vendor blogs quote indicative day rates roughly like this.

items: Commercial models: about ₹10,000 to ₹50,000 a day
Fashion models: about ₹20,000 to ₹1,00,000 a day
Print models: about ₹5,000 to ₹25,000 a day

layout.content: Treat these as starting points for budgeting, not a rate card. Newer faces may quote below these ranges, and established names sit well above them. Half-day rates exist but are often a large share of the full day, so compare carefully.
The important point is what the base fee covers. In most quotes it pays for the model's time on set and nothing more. How the pictures can be used is priced separately.
The day rate buys the model's time. The usage fee buys your right to publish. Budget for both from the first quote.
What a usage buyout is

A usage buyout is the fee you pay for the right to use the images in specific media, for a specific territory and period. Vendor-quoted buyouts for ads, TV or outdoor can add anywhere from about ₹5,000 to well over ₹1,00,000 on top of the day rate, depending on reach and duration.
A simple way to think about usage is in tiers, each one wider and usually more expensive than the last.

items: Organic social: the brand's own Instagram, Facebook and LinkedIn posts, not boosted
Owned digital and e-commerce: website, marketplace listings, quick-commerce and catalogue pages
Paid digital: boosted posts, Meta and Google ads, YouTube pre-roll, marketplace ads
Print and out-of-home: brochures, packaging, in-store standees, hoardings, transit ads
TV and cinema: broadcast, OTT ad slots and theatrical

layout.content: For each tier, agree the territory (India only, specific states, or worldwide) and duration (six months, one year, two years). Perpetual, all-media buyouts are possible but should be priced and written explicitly, not assumed.
What to put in writing before shoot day
Most brand-model disputes come from things that were said on a call but never confirmed. A one-page booking confirmation, signed or accepted on email before the shoot, should cover these points.

items: Shoot date, studio address and call time
Working hours included, and when the clock starts (call time, not first frame)
Overtime rate per hour and who approves it on set
Number of looks or outfits, and whether hair and make-up resets count as looks
Product category, so the model can flag conflicts
Usage scope: media tiers, territory and period
Exclusivity: whether the model can work for competing brands, in which category and for how long
Fees: day rate, usage fee, travel or conveyance, and any cancellation charges
Payment terms: timeline, invoicing, GST if applicable and TDS deduction
Who holds the release, and how renewals of usage will be priced

layout.content: On catalogue days, the number of looks matters as much as the hours. Throughput varies a lot by category and styling. Some e-commerce teams report getting through dozens of simple looks in a day, while styled fashion looks move much more slowly. Agree a realistic number with your photographer and stylist, then write it into the booking.
If it is not in the confirmation email, assume it was not agreed.
Model releases: what they should include
A model release is the document in which the model grants permission for their likeness to be used. For brand work it should be specific rather than generic.

items: Names and details of the parties: the model (and agency, if any), the brand, and the agency or production company
Description of the shoot: date, location, product and type of content
Media covered, matching the usage tiers agreed
Territory and duration of use
Fee and what it covers
Whether images can be retouched, cropped or combined with other content
Signatures and date; a guardian's signature for anyone under 18

layout.content: Collect releases on the day, before the model leaves the studio. Chasing a signature weeks later, after the images are already live, puts the brand in a weak position.
Model agencies vs freelancers

Model agencies in Delhi NCR and Mumbai usually handle quotes, contracts, invoicing and releases, and they will flag usage and exclusivity issues upfront. That adds a fee but removes a lot of admin, and an agency can often send a replacement if a model falls ill.

Freelance models, often found through Instagram or casting platforms, can be quicker and more affordable for simple catalogue work. The trade-off is that the brand or production house has to do the paperwork itself: written confirmation, release, payment and TDS.

items: For paid campaigns, outdoor and TV, an agency booking usually gives cleaner paperwork
For organic social and catalogue, a well-documented freelancer booking can work well
Either way, the brand should keep a copy of the signed release and usage terms

layout.content: FAQs: model fees and usage rights
How much does a model charge per day in India?

Model platforms and vendor blogs quote indicative ranges of roughly ₹10,000 to ₹50,000 a day for commercial models, ₹20,000 to ₹1,00,000 for fashion and ₹5,000 to ₹25,000 for print. Actual quotes depend on experience, agency and usage.
What is a usage buyout?
It is the fee paid for the right to publish the images in agreed media, territory and duration. The base day rate usually covers only time on set, so usage is priced on top.
Do I need a model release for Instagram ads?
Paid ads are commercial use, so a signed release that covers paid digital use is strongly advisable, even if you already had permission for organic posts. Check with a lawyer for your situation.
How much does it cost to hire a model for a day of catalogue shoots?

Budget the day rate, any e-commerce or marketplace usage fee, overtime cover and conveyance. Then add studio hours, the photographer, stylist and hair and make-up. Get itemised quotes so you can compare like for like.

Final takeaways
Model fees are rarely the problem; undocumented usage is. Agree time, looks, usage and payment in writing before shoot day, and collect a specific release before the model leaves.

items: Ask every model or agency to quote day rate and usage separately
Decide your usage tiers, territory and period before booking
Send a written confirmation covering hours, overtime, looks, exclusivity and TDS
Collect signed releases on set
Have a lawyer review your standard contract and release template
